panels.title: Network TPS (non-vote)
panels.description: Transactions per second decoded from turbine shreds, excluding votes. This is what the cluster is actually processing, seen before the block is confirmed.

panels.title: Vote TPS
panels.description: Vote transactions per second. Solana's headline TPS number usually includes these.

panels.title: Block time
panels.description: Seconds per slot, measured from the arrival of the first shred of each slot.

panels.title: Current slot
panels.description: Highest slot seen on the wire.

panels.title: Turbine peers
panels.description: Peers seen in gossip that can relay to us, and peers actually sending us shreds. Zero senders means we are not in the turbine tree.

panels.title: Shred loss
panels.description: Share of data shreds never received before their slot aged out, out of every shred the slot should have had. Erasure-recovered shreds count as received, so this is the loss that survived recovery: anything above zero means the TPS and transaction feed are undercounting. What turbine dropped before recovery is on 'Shred loss before and after recovery'.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_missing_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(sniper_shreds_received_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_recovered_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_missing_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)), 0.001)

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: Throughput observed on the wire, split by kind. Non-vote is the number that matters for a sniper.

panels.title: Entry availability latency
panels.description: Time from a batch's first shred landing on our socket to its transactions being decoded. This is the head start over RPC.

panels.title: Turbine ingest
panels.description: Datagrams read from the TVU sockets, and how they split between usable data shreds and everything else (coding shreds, repair traffic, junk).

panels.title: Shred loss and duplicates
panels.description: Shreds that never arrived before their slot aged out, and shreds delivered more than once by the turbine tree.

panels.title: Slot duration
panels.description: Distribution of wall time between consecutive slots, as seen from the shreds.

panels.title: Pipeline backlog
panels.description: Packets waiting to be parsed, slots held in the assembler, and per-packet parse time. A growing queue means the parser is falling behind the sockets.

panels.title: Batches and snipe hits
panels.description: Entry batches reassembled per second by outcome, plus transactions matching SNIPE_PROGRAM. Sustained 'failed' means the shred layout drifted.

panels.title: Slot coverage
panels.description: Median share of a slot's data shreds we actually saw, measured against the count the slot's closing shred declares. This is the product: everything downstream can only be as complete as this.

panels.title: Kernel drops
panels.description: Datagrams the kernel discarded before we could read them. Nothing else on this dashboard moves when this does: an overflowing receive buffer looks exactly like a quiet network.

panels.title: Opaque transactions
panels.description: Share of transactions reaching programs through an address lookup table. We cannot resolve those, so a snipe target behind one is missed rather than misreported: this is the size of that blind spot.

panels.title: Snipe latency within slot
panels.description: How far into the slot we were when a snipe hit surfaced, measured from the slot's first shred. A hit at 350 ms of a 400 ms slot is worthless; the count of hits alone never says which kind we got.

panels.title: Slot coverage distribution
panels.description: Coverage across slots. The low quantiles are the interesting ones: a p50 of 100% with a p01 of 80% means a fifth of some slots is routinely invisible to us.

panels.title: Delivery skew vs leader clock
panels.description: Arrival offset within the slot minus the offset the leader stamped into the shred's reference tick. The two clocks share no origin, so the absolute value means nothing — the spread is turbine delivery jitter, and widening is what to watch.

panels.title: Ingest pressure
panels.description: Early warning, in the order it fires: the queue peak rises first, then receivers start allocating because the parser has not returned a batch, and only then does the kernel begin dropping. Slots without a closing shred ride along as a coverage caveat.

panels.title: Batch latency by path
panels.description: Entry batch latency split by whether the batch had to wait on erasure recovery. The gap between the two lines is what recovery costs us in time, as opposed to what it saves us in shreds.

panels.title: Read batching
panels.description: Datagrams returned per recvmmsg call. Piled up at one means the syscall amortizes nothing and the socket is idle between packets; mass at 64 means we are reading at line rate.

panels.title: Erasure recovery
panels.description: Data shreds rebuilt from their erasure batch, against the ones that stayed lost and the batches that could not be repaired at all. Recovery is the only thing standing between turbine dropping a shred and us never seeing its transactions: without it, 'recovered' would be added to 'still missing'.

panels.title: Shred loss before and after recovery
panels.description: What turbine failed to deliver, and what was still missing once Reed-Solomon had done its work. Both are measured against every data shred the slot should have had, so the gap between the lines is exactly what recovery bought us. Note this differs from the 'Shred loss' stat above, which leaves recovered shreds out of its denominator.

targets.expr: ((sum(rate(sniper_shreds_recovered_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_missing_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0))) / clamp_min(sum(rate(sniper_shreds_received_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_recovered_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_missing_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)), 0.001)

(sum(rate(sniper_shreds_missing_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(sniper_shreds_received_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_recovered_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(sniper_shreds_missing_total{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)), 0.001)

panels.title: Bot vs wallet, by slot
panels.description: One row per slot where either side traded. tx_gap is how many transactions separate the bot from the wallet inside the block. Reacting to a transaction can only land behind it, so a bot that snipes this wallet has a positive gap and small is good; a negative one means the bot fired on its own rather than in response. same_entry means the two share an entry, and transactions of one entry execute in parallel — the gap is still real but it does not order them. exact is false when a batch we never decoded sits between the two, which makes the count short by whatever it held. Until the bot exists, every row carries the wallet's signature alone, which is the baseline it will be judged against.

panels.title: Watched wallet
panels.description: Transactions per second paid for by a wallet in TARGET_WALLETS. Zero means either the wallet is idle or the address is wrong — nothing else on this row can be read until this one moves.

panels.title: Slot left, typical
panels.description: What is left of the slot by the time the wallet's transaction is decoded here. This is the entire budget for reacting to it and landing in the same block: everything a sniper would have to do — decide, sign, send, and reach the leader — has to fit inside this number. The slot's length is the measured one rather than mainnet's 400 ms, so the reading stays honest on a cluster that runs slower.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(sniper_slot_duration_seconds_bucket{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval]))) - histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(sniper_watched_offset_seconds_bucket{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Slot left, worst 5%
panels.description: The same budget in the slowest twentieth of cases. A sniper is judged on this rather than on the median: the trades worth taking are the ones nobody else got to, and those are exactly the ones that surfaced late.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(sniper_slot_duration_seconds_bucket{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval]))) - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(sniper_watched_offset_seconds_bucket{job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Watched wallet within the slot
panels.description: Where in the slot the wallet's transactions surface, measured from our own first shred of that slot. The slot's own length is drawn alongside: a quantile touching that line is a transaction that left no room to answer it in the same block. The gap between p50 and p99 is what a reaction budget has to survive.
